fields.meta_title: News Landing Page Builder for Newsrooms | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a news landing page from a prompt: a breaking banner, beat pages readers follow, a tip form, and a live updates feed. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a News Landing Page That Leads With What Just Happened
fields.hero_description: Build a news landing page that puts breaking stories on top and saves every story and reader tip to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Newsroom Gets From One Prompt
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the news landing page readers see and the tools editors use to run it through a busy news day.
fields.feature_1:
Sections laid out from your prompt

Name the sections you publish, such as Local, Schools and Sports, and Emergent builds a row for each with the newest story first. Adding a section later takes one more prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A breaking banner editors control

An editor flags a story as breaking and the app shows it in a banner above every section. Clearing the flag removes the banner, and the story stays in its own section.
fields.feature_3:
Every story is a row you own

Each story is saved with its byline and publish time to a database you own. The archive page, the search page and any export you run all read from that one shared table.
fields.feature_4:
Email when a beat gets a story

The app can email each reader who follows a beat as soon as a story is filed under it, and alert the news desk by email or in Slack the moment a reader sends in a tip.
fields.feature_5:
Connected to the tools you use

Connect the page to any tool with an API, such as Slack for the desk or the CMS where your reporters file, and stories and tips sync in and out without copy and paste.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code too

Publish the page on your own domain: custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and build on it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
A breaking banner sits above every section

When an editor at the Brindle County Courier flags a story as breaking, the front page opens on a banner. At 2:15 p.m. it read Route 9 bridge closed after a crash. Below it, the Local, Schools, Business, and Sports rows each show their 3 newest stories. Clearing the flag takes the banner down.
fields.tab_content_2:
Readers who follow a beat get each new story by email

Cold Chain Weekly covers refrigerated freight, and its Food Safety beat page has 214 followers, each signed up with the Follow button on that page. When an editor tags a new story Food Safety, the app emails all 214 a link to it and moves the story to the top of the beat page.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each tip goes to the editor who owns that section

Readers of the Oakridge Lantern pick a section before they send a news tip. Sports tips go to Tomasz Wielgosz and Campus tips go to Junia Halvorsen, by email. A tip about shorter Sunday dining hall hours reached Junia at 9:12 p.m., saved with its section and the time it came in.
fields.tab_content_4:
The newest update appears first, with its time

During a storm, the Marlow Bay Gazette runs one live updates page instead of filing a new story every hour. Since 6:00 a.m. it has posted 12 updates, newest first, each with a time stamp. The 9:40 a.m. post, Shelter opens at the Harbor Street library, appeared at the top of every open copy of the page without a reload.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a News Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a news landing page around your sections and breaking stories, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the page leads with
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List your sections in reading order
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the rule for breaking news
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write the prompt with real headlines
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the one thing a reader should see first on a normal day: the top story, the latest headlines, or today's edition. Then decide what replaces it on a big news day. The top slot needs a clear owner before anything breaks.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down every section you publish and put them in the order readers scan them. A county paper might lead with Local and Schools; a trade title might lead with its two busiest beats. Cut any section you update less than once a week.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide who can flag a story as breaking, what the banner says, and when it comes down. Write it as one sentence that names who flags and who clears. A morning banner still up at 9 p.m. reads as news that never ended.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the page to Emergent using this week's actual headlines and bylines instead of made-up ones. Real headlines show you how long titles wrap on the grid and whether each section row holds the stories you expect it to.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose what readers can do besides read: follow a beat, send a tip, or open a live updates page during a storm. Name who gets each tip or alert by email, and say which fields every tip has to include before it can be sent.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Open the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a phone and read the top story and one full section with your thumb. Check that headlines stay readable, the banner does not push the first story off the screen, and the tip form fits without zooming.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page, then send a test tip and flag a test story as breaking to confirm both work. Clear the test flag, delete the test tip from the database, and share the link with the newsroom before the next edition goes up.

faq_plan.q: What is a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: A news landing page is the page a publication's readers arrive on: the front page of a news site, or the page for one section or one big story. It opens on the most important story of the hour, then lists the latest headlines by section, each linking to the full article.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Name your sections, how many stories each row shows, and which editors can turn on the breaking banner. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it, and you change any part of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should go at the top of a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: The one story that matters most right now, with its headline, a one-line summary, and the time it was last updated. Put the latest headlines by section below it. On a day with breaking news, let a banner above everything take the top spot until an editor clears it.

faq_plan.q: Should a news landing page cover one event or the whole site?
faq_plan.a: Both work, for different jobs. The front page covers the whole site. A page built for one event, such as election night or a storm, keeps every update in one place. Readers who arrive from a shared link find the whole story there. A tour operator builds a travel landing page for each trip for the same reason.

faq_plan.q: How do I show breaking news on a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: Put it in a one-line strip at the top of the page, shown only while an editor has the story flagged as breaking. Include the headline and the time, link it to the full story, and give it a stronger color than anything else on the page.

faq_plan.q: How many stories should a news landing page show?
faq_plan.a: No number fits every publication. Start with 3 stories per section row, enough for a reader to scan on a phone, and add more only if readers click past them. Emergent builds the page from a prompt, and changing the count later is one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Does a news landing page need a separate page for each section?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once a section publishes often enough to fill one. A section page lists only the stories tagged with that section, newest first. A reader who wants Sports lands on Sports and nothing else. It works like a category landing page on a store: the tag decides what appears, and a story with two tags shows on both pages.

faq_plan.q: How do readers send news tips through a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: Through a short tip form on the page: a description field, a section picker, and an optional contact field for readers who want a reply. The app can email each tip to the editor who covers that section and keep every tip in one table you can sort by section.

faq_plan.q: Can a news landing page update live during a breaking story?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A live updates page adds each short post at the top, newest first, with its time stamp. An app built with Emergent can show those updates in real time: a reader who already has the page open sees each new post without reloading it.

faq_plan.q: Can I list newsroom job openings on a news landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a small Careers link in the header or footer that points to a separate jobs page. Keep the front page for news. A full hiring page with each role and an application form fits better as one of the recruiting landing pages Emergent builds, with every application kept in a database you own.

plan.angle: The results for this keyword are design galleries, vector stock and template stores that show how a news front page looks, plus a roundup of well-known news site designs; none shows a page that a newsroom actually runs each day. This page shows four news landing pages a county paper, a trade publication, a student newspaper and a coastal daily build from a prompt, and follows what each does after it goes up: a breaking banner an editor pins above every section, a beat page that emails its followers when a story is tagged, a tip form that routes each tip to the section editor, and a live updates page for a storm that adds each post at the top. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what leads, section pages, breaking news, story counts, tips, live coverage and newsroom job openings.
